scope: Current merged User Administration, Developer Workload, Business Catalog, My Notifications, access email, and Bug email behavior. Existing catalog keys stay internal; every new proposal is a NOT_RUN candidate.

features.objective: Trace the active-PM/UserAdmin boundary, onboarding and SAP identity verification, access lifecycle, identity-link lifecycle, and operation recovery.

implementedBehaviors.description: XSUAA origin, issuer, and subject map to one active IDTS user and reject unmapped, multi-role, or role-mismatched identities.
Existing security coverage maps public projections and sanitized errors to the User Administration boundary.
Existing security coverage keeps failed User Administration operations free of partial mutation.
Task 2 retains the allowed-role matrix candidate covering TESTER, DEVELOPER, and PM checks.
Every User Administration administrative read or action requires exactly one PM business role, the UserAdmin capability, and an active internal requester.
An authorized PM creates a normalized expiring invitation, persists only token material, stores the desired access/profile, and creates one pending delivery.
A matching SAP identity consumes an invitation once and moves standard access to a queued operation while keeping identity internals out of the public result.
Tampered or mismatched invitation claims fail closed before request consumption or access-operation creation.
Onboarding search returns bounded safe summaries with latest operation attempts and server-owned cancellation eligibility.
PM/UserAdmin approval changes only the expected request version, queues provisioning, and appends an audit event.
Role change suspends local access and sessions before provider reconciliation and records the desired operation without claiming provider completion.
Local suspension moves ACTIVE access to SUSPENDED, revokes active sessions, writes applied audit, and leaves an access-delivery source.
Reactivation queues a read-only provider operation while the local user remains inactive until verified completion.
A legacy TESTER or DEVELOPER link targets one explicit eligible row, snapshots its role/email, supports cancellation, and preserves request history.
Retry and reconcile are state-, result-, and optimistic-version-gated and rotate the operation correlation state safely.

proposedCases.title: User Administration administrative reads require the full gate
plannedAssertions: An anonymous, non-PM, PM-without-UserAdmin, or inactive requester is rejected with USER_ADMIN_REQUIRED before an administrative read or action.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Exactly one PM business role plus UserAdmin and an active internal identity are required; UserAdmin is not a fourth business role.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use pure authorization and isolated CAP request fixtures; do not call a provider or mutate onboarding, identity, catalog, or live data.

proposedCases.title: authorized onboarding request persists normalized safe state
plannedAssertions: A PM/UserAdmin onboarding request persists normalized email/display name, a token hash, the desired profile, and one PENDING delivery without exposing token internals.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only an active PM UserAdmin may create an invitation; requested business role and Developer-profile rules are server validated.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Run in an isolated CAP SQLite fixture with deterministic signing configuration; no provider, email send, BTP, or live-data mutation.

proposedCases.title: matching SAP identity verifies one onboarding invitation
plannedAssertions: A valid invitation with a matching SAP identity is consumed once, queues standard access, records one operation/audit, and omits identity fields from the result.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The signed-in SAP identity must match the invitation email and immutable identity tuple; approval remains required for PM or UserAdmin access.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use an isolated CAP fixture and deterministic signed token; do not invoke the broker or create a platform identity.

proposedCases.title: tampered invitation is rejected before consumption
plannedAssertions: A tampered invitation signature returns INVALID_INVITATION and leaves the invitation unconsumed with no access operation.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Invitation verification is claim-bound and does not grant access based on a client-supplied email or token fragment alone.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use pure token fixtures and an isolated persistence readback; no SAP login, provider, email, or live data.

proposedCases.title: mismatched SAP identity is denied without consuming invitation
plannedAssertions: A valid token used by a different normalized SAP email returns INVITATION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH and leaves the invitation INVITED with consumedAt null.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Identity email must match the invitation; the callback cannot choose another target user or bypass the immutable identity check.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated token and request fixtures; no broker, provider, email, or live identity mutation.

proposedCases.title: onboarding search returns safe status and cancellation eligibility
plannedAssertions: An authorized onboarding search returns bounded summaries and cancelEligible only for an unconsumed INVITED request, without identity or token fields.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may inspect onboarding summaries; returned rows exclude identity-link internals and token material.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use deterministic local CAP rows and read-only queries; no invitation send, provider call, or live mutation.

proposedCases.title: provisioning approval succeeds at the current version
plannedAssertions: Approval of one current-version PENDING_APPROVAL request queues provisioning, inserts one PENDING operation, and appends one audit.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Approval is a PM/UserAdmin action and never makes an operation ACTIVE without later provider readback.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Run with isolated CAP rows and transaction readback; do not contact the access broker or platform.

proposedCases.title: stale provisioning approval is rejected without mutation
plannedAssertions: Approval with a stale request version returns the safe version conflict and leaves request, operation, and audit state unchanged.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Approval is a PM/UserAdmin action and never makes an operation ACTIVE without later provider readback.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Run with isolated CAP rows and transaction readback; do not contact the access broker or platform.

proposedCases.title: role change fails closed before provider reconciliation
plannedAssertions: An authorized role change marks local access inactive, revokes active sessions, queues CHANGE_ROLE, and leaves provider completion unclaimed.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may request a role change; local authorization is reduced before any external reconciliation.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use an isolated CAP fixture and inspect user/session/request/operation rows; no broker or live role-collection write.

proposedCases.title: local suspension revokes sessions and creates its access delivery
plannedAssertions: Suspending an ACTIVE user changes local state to SUSPENDED, revokes every unrevoked session, records QUEUED then APPLIED audit rows, and creates the APPLIED SUSPEND access delivery.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may suspend access; the final active UserAdmin remains protected.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use a deterministic local CAP transaction and readback; do not call provider, send email, or mutate shared data.

proposedCases.title: reactivation stays inactive until queued operation completes
plannedAssertions: Reactivation increments the request version and queues REACTIVATE while the local user remains inactive until provider proof.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may request reactivation; the provider operation must later prove the immutable identity and desired role collections.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated suspended user/request/session rows; no provider, email, BTP, or live-data operation.

proposedCases.title: legacy identity link snapshots one eligible target
plannedAssertions: An eligible legacy TESTER or DEVELOPER links exactly one selected Users.ID and snapshots its role and source email into one pending link request.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may link an active legacy TESTER/DEVELOPER row; already-linked, partial-identity, PM, inactive, and nonlegacy targets are rejected.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use an isolated CAP SQLite fixture; do not verify a real SAP identity or create a provider account.

proposedCases.title: cancelling an unverified invitation preserves history
plannedAssertions: Cancelling an unconsumed INVITED request marks its delivery SKIPPED, releases its open-request key, appends one audit event, and preserves history rows.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may cancel and only before SAP identity verification; stale versions or consumed requests are rejected.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated request and delivery fixtures with transaction readback; no email send, provider, or live-data mutation.

proposedCases.title: retry accepts only a bounded retryable access failure
plannedAssertions: Retry accepts only a bounded retryable access-operation failure with the expected version, resets it to PENDING with a new correlation, and appends one audit.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only an authorized PM/UserAdmin may retry its own server-selected retryable access operation.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use an isolated local operation fixture and transaction; no provider, email, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: reconcile accepts only an ambiguous provider outcome
plannedAssertions: Reconcile accepts only AMBIGUOUS_PROVIDER_OUTCOME with the expected version, creates a fresh correlation, and appends one audit without accepting an unrelated outcome.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only an authorized PM/UserAdmin may reconcile the server-selected ambiguous access operation.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use an isolated local operation fixture and transaction; no provider, email, BTP, or live data.

features.objective: Trace safe active-user display-name administration and Developer Profile validation, persistence, optimistic versioning, and audit.

implementedBehaviors.description: PM/UserAdmin can read the active Developer profile result with readiness, responsibility, and open-bug impact fields; inactive Developer targets fail safely.
PM/UserAdmin updates only displayName with a reason and expected modifiedAt, then records USER_PROFILE_UPDATED without changing email or identity fields.
Developer Profile updates validate active catalogs, update availability/workload, deactivate removed responsibilities, reuse matching rows, and append bounded audit actions.

Developer profile input normalization requires a positive workload limit, nonduplicate component/module scope tuples, at least one responsibility for DEVELOPER access, and no profile for non-DEVELOPER access.

proposedCases.title: active-user display name update preserves identity fields
plannedAssertions: A valid PM/UserAdmin display-name update persists the normalized name and one audit reason while email, role, active state, and identity fields remain unchanged after reload.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only the active PM/UserAdmin administrator may update another active user profile; client identity or email fields are not accepted as mutation inputs.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use the existing isolated CAP SQLite active-user fixture; no provider, email, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: stale display name version is rejected without mutation
plannedAssertions: A display-name update with an old modifiedAt returns USER_PROFILE_VERSION_CONFLICT and leaves the stored user and audit count unchanged.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The PM/UserAdmin action uses server-owned optimistic concurrency; a stale dialog cannot overwrite a newer profile update.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use an isolated CAP row with before/after readback; no external integration or live mutation.

proposedCases.title: Developer Profile update persists responsibility lifecycle
plannedAssertions: A valid Developer Profile update persists availability/workload, deactivates removed responsibilities without deletion, and writes bounded administration audits after reload.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may administer an active Developer Profile; existing assigned Bugs are not reassigned by profile changes.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use an isolated CAP SQLite fixture with catalog rows and persistence readback; no provider or live data.

proposedCases.title: profile workload limit rejects nonpositive input
plannedAssertions: normalizeDeveloperProfileInput rejects a zero or negative workloadLimit with INVALID_DEVELOPER_WORKLOAD_LIMIT.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only Developer access may carry a profile; responsibility levels and UUID references are allowlisted before catalog lookup.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use pure local normalization fixtures; no CAP database, external service, or live data.

proposedCases.title: profile responsibilities reject duplicate scope tuples
plannedAssertions: normalizeDeveloperProfileInput rejects two responsibilities with the same componentCategoryID and sapModuleID scope, regardless of responsibility level, with DUPLICATE_DEVELOPER_RESPONSIBILITY.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only Developer access may carry a profile; responsibility levels and UUID references are allowlisted before catalog lookup.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use pure local normalization fixtures; no CAP database, external service, or live data.

proposedCases.title: Developer access requires one responsibility
plannedAssertions: assertDeveloperProfileForRole rejects a DEVELOPER role with no responsibility using DEVELOPER_PROFILE_REQUIRED.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only Developer access may carry a profile; responsibility levels and UUID references are allowlisted before catalog lookup.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use pure local normalization fixtures; no CAP database, external service, or live data.

proposedCases.title: non-Developer access cannot own a Developer Profile
plannedAssertions: assertDeveloperProfileForRole rejects a non-DEVELOPER role with a profile using DEVELOPER_PROFILE_NOT_ALLOWED.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only Developer access may carry a profile; responsibility levels and UUID references are allowlisted before catalog lookup.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use pure local normalization fixtures; no CAP database, external service, or live data.

features.objective: Trace the read-only DeveloperWorkloads aggregate, identity readiness, server-authoritative scope, numeric derivation, and safe UI drill-down.

implementedBehaviors.description: Approved monitoring cases already cover due-date overdue boundaries, non-Closed open counts, threshold overload, current-action totals, and deterministic search/order.
The server resolves the actor before client search/filter/count/paging and a Developer cannot widen its own row scope.
Task 2 retains the due-date boundary evaluation for workload monitoring.
The aggregate exposes identityAccessReady from the bounded identity-readiness helper and fails closed for unmapped, inactive, or mismatched identities.
The read model rounds decimal effort in memory, keeps an active zero-load Developer visible, and retains inactive/backlog rows without writing aggregate data.
The UI loads only non-Closed assigned Bugs with technical assignee/current action owner fields, safe columns, and an allowlisted active Bug deep link.
Task 2 retains PM operational-metrics authorization as a separate approved candidate.

proposedCases.title: Developer workload identity readiness fails closed

sourceTrace.symbol: Duplicate matching ACTIVE requests are not ready

plannedAssertions: A workload row is ready only for one exact linked active identity; unmapped, inactive, hash-mismatched, and duplicate-active-request identities are not ready.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: PM may see all workload rows; Developer scope remains server-resolved and identity readiness is never inferred from client filters or platform role text.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use deterministic local CAP fixtures and bounded identity helper reads; no identity provider, BTP, write, or live data.

proposedCases.title: workload aggregates decimal effort without mutation
plannedAssertions: The workload row sums Decimal/string effort to two decimals while persisted Bug effort values remain unchanged after the read.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: This is a read-only aggregate for PM or the server-resolved Developer; no caller may update Bug ownership or effort through the workload endpoint.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated SQLite rows with decimal strings and before/after readback; no external integration or live mutation.

proposedCases.title: zero-load and inactive backlog workload rows remain truthful
plannedAssertions: An active Developer with zero open Bugs remains visible, an inactive Developer with an open backlog remains visible, and an inactive zero-backlog row is omitted.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: PM monitoring may show active and backlog-bearing inactive profiles; Developer reads remain limited to the active actor's server-resolved row.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local profile/Bug fixtures and read-only aggregation; no reassignment, write, or live data.

proposedCases.title: workload drill-down excludes Closed Bugs and uses safe deep links
plannedAssertions: The drill-down requests only the selected profile’s non-Closed Bugs, keeps technical assignee and current action owner distinct, and creates a deep link only for a valid active entity UUID.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The UI is read-only and the backend remains authoritative for assigned Bug visibility; no UI control changes Bug ownership.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: The existing controller/UI contract is a programmatic precheck only; final acceptance requires browser/runtime rendered UI execution and screenshot(s) of the workload drill-down; no Bug mutation, BTP, or live data.
evidenceRequirements: Run the existing programmatic/native-control harness as a precheck only; harness output cannot establish visual acceptance.
Execute the application in a browser/runtime with the rendered UI for this case.
Capture at least one case-specific screenshot of the rendered UI state and retain the runtime URL/route context.

features.objective: Trace catalog projections, PM/UserAdmin authorization, normalized CRUD, immutable keys, impact checks, pair validation, audit, and safe UI controls.

implementedBehaviors.description: The approved validation cases cover code-list unknown/inactive/type/format rejection and component-category derivation, mismatch, change, and partial classification boundaries.
Existing security coverage rejects client writes to read-only catalog code-list entities.
Application Component/Defect Category create, non-PM authorization, active parent validation, and inactive priority classification were retained or rewritten in Task 2 rather than duplicated here.

SAP Module and Component Category create, safe reads, immutable ID/ETag update, deactivation blocking for active responsibility or child references, impact readback, and no-delete behavior are implemented but not atomic in the approved catalog.

proposedCases.title: PM creates normalized SAP Module catalog row
plannedAssertions: PM/UserAdmin CREATE of CatalogSAPModules normalizes code/name, assigns a server UUID, persists active state, and records one safe CREATE audit after reload.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may create catalog rows; IDs and audit actor are server-owned.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated CAP SQLite catalog fixtures; no canonical catalog, dependency, BTP, or live-data mutation.

proposedCases.title: PM creates one valid Component Category pair
plannedAssertions: CREATE of one nonduplicate Component Category with two active parents persists one pair with a server UUID and a safe audit.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active PM/UserAdmin may create pair catalog rows; parent activity and pair uniqueness are server checks.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local ApplicationComponent, DefectCategory, and ComponentCategory rows; no Bug or live catalog mutation.

proposedCases.title: catalog read exposes safe rows only to PM UserAdmin
plannedAssertions: PM/UserAdmin receives only the declared catalog projection fields, while unauthorized callers receive 403 before a catalog table read.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Catalog administration requires active PM plus UserAdmin; business roles cannot be widened by an extra or mixed role.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use CDS metadata and isolated read fixtures only; no write, seed, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: catalog update rejects route and payload ID conflict
plannedAssertions: An update whose route ID differs from its payload ID returns the documented safe identity conflict and leaves the catalog row unchanged.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only PM/UserAdmin may update; the route key and server ETag, not client payload identity, select the target.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated SQLite catalog row with before/after/audit readback; no live catalog or dependency mutation.

proposedCases.title: catalog update rejects a stale ETag
plannedAssertions: An update with a stale If-Match returns the documented optimistic conflict and leaves the catalog row and audit unchanged.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only PM/UserAdmin may update; the route key and server ETag, not client payload identity, select the target.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated SQLite catalog row with before/after/audit readback; no live catalog or dependency mutation.

proposedCases.title: catalog deactivation blocks active responsibility or child references
plannedAssertions: A deactivation with an approved reason returns CATALOG_HAS_ACTIVE_DEPENDENCIES when active responsibility or child-reference counts are nonzero, while bugReferenceCount remains informational and the row is unchanged.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only a PM/UserAdmin administrative action may request catalog deactivation; server-read active responsibility and child-reference counts decide the block.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local catalog, responsibility, child-reference, and Bug-reference fixtures; no canonical catalog or live data.

proposedCases.title: catalog impact returns bounded counts
plannedAssertions: readCatalogImpact returns catalogType/catalogID plus Bug, active responsibility, and active child-reference counts for a supported target and rejects invalid targets safely.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only PM/UserAdmin may read catalog impact; the operation is diagnostic and does not change dependency state.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated CAP rows and read-only aggregate queries; no deactivation, write, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: catalog DELETE is forbidden
plannedAssertions: DELETE returns CATALOG_DELETE_FORBIDDEN and leaves the catalog row present and unchanged.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only PM/UserAdmin may request catalog updates; no caller may hard-delete historical catalog rows.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated catalog fixtures and transaction readback; no canonical catalog, Bug, or live-data mutation.

proposedCases.title: catalog reactivation is audited
plannedAssertions: A valid inactive-to-active update persists REACTIVATE and exactly one safe audit event after reload.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only PM/UserAdmin may request catalog updates; no caller may hard-delete historical catalog rows.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated catalog fixtures and transaction readback; no canonical catalog, Bug, or live-data mutation.

features.objective: Trace caller-only inbox search, hydration, read-state mutation, source isolation, safe deep links, and native shell loading/error/empty behavior.

implementedBehaviors.description: Eligible Bug workflow events create in-app notifications and rejected workflow actions create no notification or delivery.
Existing security coverage keeps public notification projections free of credential and lock fields.
Existing security coverage keeps failed notification operations free of cross-entity partial mutation.
The NotificationService exposes caller-only category/read-state paging with stable ordering and a safe Bug/access DTO, but the approved catalog has no atomic inbox case.
The native shell renders compact Bug-title rows without a redundant icon/description, freezes mark-all snapshots, and exposes loading/empty/error/retry states without horizontal scrolling.

proposedCases.title: My Notifications search is caller-scoped and stably ordered
plannedAssertions: The inbox returns only the authenticated caller’s rows, applies bounded filters and paging, and orders rows by occurredAt desc then ID desc for equal timestamps.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: An active identity may read only its own inbox; PM/UserAdmin does not grant access to another user's personal notifications.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated CAP inbox/source fixtures and OData service calls; no notification delivery, email, provider, or live data.

proposedCases.title: My Notifications hydration isolates source summaries
plannedAssertions: A mixed page hydrates Bug and applied-access sources into the safe DTO, with UNAVAILABLE and null targetPath for wrong-recipient, dual-source, unsupported, or missing sources.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Hydration binds each source to the inbox recipient; raw audit details, recipient email, identity, and provider fields never enter the DTO.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated source rows and read-only hydration; no mark-read, email, provider, or live mutation.

proposedCases.title: unread count is isolated to the active caller
plannedAssertions: getMyUnreadNotificationCount counts only unread rows for the resolved active caller and denies inactive, unmapped, or unauthorized identities.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Caller identity comes from the authenticated request and cannot be supplied as a recipient parameter.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated CAP inbox rows and service calls; no write, email, provider, or live data.

proposedCases.title: single notification read succeeds with current version
plannedAssertions: A caller marks its own unread row read with the exact current modifiedAt and the persisted row is read after reload.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only the inbox owner may mark a row read; notification ID and modifiedAt are validated server-side.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated CAP row with before/after/reload readback; no provider, email, or live data.

proposedCases.title: repeated notification read is idempotent
plannedAssertions: Repeating the same notification read with the already-applied version returns the same safe result without changing the row again.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only the inbox owner may mark a row read; notification ID and modifiedAt are validated server-side.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated CAP row with before/after/reload readback; no provider, email, or live data.

proposedCases.title: stale notification read is rejected
plannedAssertions: A notification read with a stale modifiedAt returns NOTIFICATION_VERSION_CONFLICT without changing the row.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only the inbox owner may mark a row read; notification ID and modifiedAt are validated server-side.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated CAP row with before/after/reload readback; no provider, email, or live data.

proposedCases.title: mark-all read honors a frozen occurrence snapshot
plannedAssertions: markAllMyNotificationsRead updates only the caller’s unread rows with occurredAt at or before throughOccurredAt, leaving a later notification unread after reload.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The operation is caller-only and cannot mark another user's inbox even for a PM/UserAdmin identity.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated inbox timestamps and transaction readback; no delivery, email, provider, or live mutation.

features.objective: Trace access-completion and onboarding email payloads, access inbox indexing, safe skip/retry behavior, and post-commit scheduling.

implementedBehaviors.description: The approved generic outbox cases cover valid pending delivery, disabled/missing/inactive recipient skips, worker claim/send, failure sanitization, retry timing, maximum attempts, and duplicate worker claims.
Applied CHANGE_ROLE or REACTIVATE completion audits create one access delivery and caller inbox index.
Applied access delivery creation applies an access-specific invalid application URL skip with a safe persisted reason.
Generic access worker claim/send mechanics are covered by shared existing outbox cases; access-specific creation and skip behavior are traced separately.
Onboarding-specific invitation eligibility, token integrity, message boundaries, cancellation state, and post-commit kick behavior are implemented but not atomic in the approved catalog.
An applied REVOKE audit maps to ACCESS_REVOKED and creates a delivery without a caller inbox index.

proposedCases.title: applied role-change completion creates one inbox index
plannedAssertions: An APPLIED CHANGE_ROLE or REACTIVATE audit creates one source-bound access delivery and one caller inbox index, while queued, failed, mismatched, or duplicate calls create no second index.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only an applied CHANGE_ROLE or REACTIVATE audit for the target user can create the completion delivery and inbox index.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local audit/delivery fixtures and transaction; no provider, email, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: applied REVOKE creates one access delivery
plannedAssertions: An APPLIED REVOKE audit with eventType ACCESS_REVOKED creates one access delivery for the target user and does not create an inbox index.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only an applied REVOKE audit for the target user can create the revoked-access delivery; inbox indexing remains server-controlled.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local audit/delivery fixtures and transaction; no provider, email, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: applied access delivery skips an invalid application URL
plannedAssertions: An APPLIED access audit with an invalid application URL creates a SKIPPED access delivery with EMAIL_BASE_URL_INVALID and makes no provider call.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only the server-created applied access audit can create this access delivery; the client cannot override the application URL.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local access audit, recipient, and invalid-URL fixtures; no provider, email, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: missing or expired onboarding invitation is skipped

sourceTrace.symbol: Invitation is no longer eligible for delivery

plannedAssertions: When the onboarding request is missing or expired, the worker marks its delivery SKIPPED with a safe code and makes no provider call.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The worker uses persisted invitation existence and expiry; a caller cannot turn a missing or expired invitation into a send.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local onboarding request/delivery fixtures and an injected sender; no real email, provider, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: token-mismatch onboarding delivery fails with bounded retry
plannedAssertions: When persisted token material does not match, the worker marks the delivery FAILED with INVITATION_TOKEN_MISMATCH, sanitizes error state, and schedules a bounded retry when attempts remain.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The worker compares regenerated invitation material with the persisted hash before sending and records only sanitized failure state.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local onboarding delivery fixtures and an injected sender; no real email, provider, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: onboarding invitation email keeps link and security boundaries

sourceTrace.symbol: IDTS will never ask for your SAP password

plannedAssertions: The invitation text and HTML use an HTTPS fragment token link plus official SAP account/registration links, omit query-token links and credentials, and preserve requested role/expiry.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The message is an invitation to SAP identity verification, not a password, OTP, provider, or email-account existence flow.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Build the message in memory with sanitized fixture data; do not send email or contact SAP.

proposedCases.title: cancelled invitation cannot be delivered

sourceTrace.symbol: Invitation is no longer eligible for delivery

plannedAssertions: After cancellation marks the delivery SKIPPED and request FAILED, a worker run makes no provider call and preserves the cancellation reason.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only an authorized administrator can cancel before verification; the worker rechecks server request state before sending.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated request/delivery rows and an injected sender; no real email, provider, or live data.

proposedCases.title: successful CAP request registers one post-commit email kick
plannedAssertions: A successful CAP request with a PENDING onboarding or access delivery registers one post-commit email outbox kick.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The kick is a server-side post-commit optimization; business callers cannot invoke the provider directly.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use the existing fake request/worker dependency harness; no real email, provider, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: repeated post-commit registration is idempotent
plannedAssertions: Registering the same PENDING delivery twice results in one post-commit email outbox kick registration.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The kick is a server-side post-commit optimization; business callers cannot invoke the provider directly.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use the existing fake request/worker dependency harness; no real email, provider, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: CAP rollback starts no provider work
plannedAssertions: A failed CAP request rolls back its post-commit registration and starts no provider work.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: The kick is a server-side post-commit optimization; business callers cannot invoke the provider directly.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use the existing fake request/worker dependency harness; no real email, provider, BTP, or live data.

features.objective: Trace Bug notification outbox behavior plus scheduled Pending Assignment/Overdue/SLA discovery, digest snapshots, bounded paging, retry, and send-time authorization.

implementedBehaviors.description: Existing notification/outbox cases cover in-app source creation, email payload creation, disabled/recipient skips, worker claim/send, retry timing, max attempts, duplicate claims, Job Scheduler authorization, and provider-error sanitization.
The scheduler discovers Pending Assignment, Critical/Blocker and standard SLA, and Overdue events with immutable history anchors, recipient rechecks, dedupe, and bounded keyset pages.
Weekday Bangkok digest snapshots role-specific actionable items, limits rendered content, uses allowlisted links, persists one recipient/date/type row, and sends with bounded persona/retry checks.

proposedCases.title: scheduled discovery emits one Pending Assignment event
plannedAssertions: The protected scheduler creates one Pending Assignment event for each eligible PM recipient and no event for a non-PM target.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only OutboxProcessor may run scheduled discovery; recipient role and active state are rechecked before source or email creation.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use deterministic local Bug/history/user fixtures and injected email configuration; no real scheduler, provider, email, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: scheduled discovery emits urgent SLA at four hours
plannedAssertions: A Critical or Blocker Pending Assignment emits its SLA event at exactly four hours and not before.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only OutboxProcessor may run scheduled discovery; recipient role and active state are rechecked before source or email creation.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use deterministic local Bug/history/user fixtures and injected email configuration; no real scheduler, provider, email, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: scheduled discovery emits standard SLA at 24 hours
plannedAssertions: A non-Critical, non-Blocker Pending Assignment emits its SLA event at exactly 24 hours and not before.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only OutboxProcessor may run scheduled discovery; recipient role and active state are rechecked before source or email creation.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use deterministic local Bug/history/user fixtures and injected email configuration; no real scheduler, provider, email, BTP, or live data.

proposedCases.title: overdue discovery excludes Closed Bugs and unsafe recipients
plannedAssertions: An overdue non-Closed Bug creates one event only for an eligible current owner or assignee, while a Closed Bug creates none.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active aligned recipients receive a scheduled event; stale or inactive current owners and profiles are excluded.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated Bug/history/profile/user fixtures and readback; no provider, email, scheduler service, or live data.

proposedCases.title: overdue discovery is idempotent for one source key
plannedAssertions: Rerunning an overdue discovery cycle with the same due-date history source key creates no duplicate event.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active aligned recipients receive a scheduled event; stale or inactive current owners and profiles are excluded.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated Bug/history/profile/user fixtures and readback; no provider, email, scheduler service, or live data.

proposedCases.title: a new due-date cycle gets a distinct source key
plannedAssertions: A changed due-date history cycle receives a distinct overdue source key from the previous cycle.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Only active aligned recipients receive a scheduled event; stale or inactive current owners and profiles are excluded.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated Bug/history/profile/user fixtures and readback; no provider, email, scheduler service, or live data.

proposedCases.title: scheduled discovery enforces the activation cutoff
plannedAssertions: A server activation cutoff excludes Pending Assignment and Overdue backlog created before scheduler activation.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Cutoff and page scope are server-controlled; client request filters cannot widen scheduled Bug discovery.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use injected local transaction/page fixtures with no external scheduler, provider, email, or live data.

proposedCases.title: scheduled discovery advances by ID keyset
plannedAssertions: The second candidate and PM page uses ID greater-than keyset ordering rather than OFFSET and remains bounded by the page limit.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Cutoff and page scope are server-controlled; client request filters cannot widen scheduled Bug discovery.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use injected local transaction/page fixtures with no external scheduler, provider, email, or live data.

proposedCases.title: scheduled page failure does not advance its cursor
plannedAssertions: A failed page transaction rolls back its writes and leaves the committed cursor unchanged so the same page can be retried.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Cutoff and page scope are server-controlled; client request filters cannot widen scheduled Bug discovery.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use injected local transaction/page fixtures with no external scheduler, provider, email, or live data.

proposedCases.title: digest snapshot selects one persona’s actionable Bugs
plannedAssertions: A PM, Developer, or Tester snapshot includes only that recipient persona’s actionable non-Closed Bugs.
proposedCases.roleBoundary: Digest persona is derived from the stored recipient role/profile at snapshot time; a client cannot supply a different role or recipient.
proposedCases.executionBoundary: Use isolated local Bug/profile/user fixtures and in-memory snapshot output; no email send, provider, scheduler, BTP, or live data.
